title: Computing resolutions, cycle classes and tensor-pairing data
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use right-derived module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and the signed total tensor convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For a nonnegative module complex, cupCycleClass sends a vector in the kernel of the outgoing differential through the canonical cycles isomorphism and homology projection. A CupAcyclicResolution of F consists of a nonnegative resolution K, its quasi-isomorphic augmentation F[0] to K, an injective resolution I, and a comparison K to I extending the augmentation and inducing isomorphisms after taking global cohomology. Its class map is the resulting homology map followed by the inverse canonical injective-resolution identification. A CupResolutionPairing of F,G consists of such computing resolutions of F,G,F tensor G and sectionwise O-linear bilinear maps in degrees r,s into degree r+s. These commute with restriction, satisfy the signed total Leibniz rule, and extend the ordinary tensor of coefficient sections through the three augmentations in degree zero. These are exactly the existing resolution-data definitions formerly in ModuleCohomologyCupProduct, moved verbatim without redefining their notions.
